The instructions include connecting water and power lines, leveling the unit using adjustable feet, installing the furniture door, and adjusting door springs. Two specific methods for securing the dishwasher are provided based on the work surface type: using an installation hook with wood screws for normal surfaces (A) or fixing the side with a screw for marble or granite tops (B). - The dishwasher is leveled by turning the rear foot with a Philips screw and the front feet with a flat screw driver.
- Door spring tension is adjusted clockwise with an Allen key.
- For normal work surfaces, use an installation hook secured with wood screws.
- For marble or granite work tops, fix the side with a Screw.

Remove any other appliances sharing the same circuit with the dishwasher.
| Power supply is not turned on. | Make sure the dishwasher is turned on and the door is closed securely.
Make sure the power cord is properly plugged into the wall socket.
| Water pressure is low | Check that the water supply is connected properly and the water is turned on.
| Door of dishwasher not properly closed. | Make sure to close the door properly and latch it.
| Water not pumped form dishwasher | Twisted or trapped drain hose. | Check the drain hose.
| Filter clogged. | Check coarse the filter.
| Kitchen sink clogged. | Check the kitchen sink to make sure it is draining well. If the problem is the kitchen sink that is not draining, you may need a plumber rather than a serviceman for dishwashers.

| Black or grey marks on dishes | Aluminium utensils have rubbed against dishes | Use a mild abrasive cleaner to eliminate those marks.

The water softener is designed to remove minerals and salts from the water, which would have a detrimental or adverse effect on the operation of the appliance. This page provides detailed recommendations for loading and unloading a dishwasher to ensure optimal performance. It includes specific guidelines on how to position various types of dishes, such as cups, glasses, and utensils, in the dishwasher baskets, emphasizing proper orientation to allow water to run off and prevent damage. The page also warns against overloading the dishwasher and advises against washing very small items that could fall out. A prominent warning box cautions users not to remove glass and cutlery for approximately 15 minutes after the program ends due to high temperatures.

**Text Evidence:**

- Items like cups, glasses, and pots/pans should be faced downwards.
- Curved items or those with recesses should be loaded at an angle to allow water to run off.
- Utensils must be stacked securely and positioned so spray arms can rotate freely.
- Hollow items should be loaded with openings facing downward to prevent water collection.
- Dishes and cutlery must not lie inside one another or cover each other.
- Glasses should not touch one another to avoid damage.
- The upper basket is designed for delicate and lighter dishware such as glasses, coffee, and tea cups.
- Long bladed knives stored upright are a potential hazard.
- Long and/or sharp cutlery items like carving knives must be positioned horizontally in the upper basket.
- Do not overload the dishwasher to ensure good results and reasonable energy consumption.
- Very small items should not be washed as they could easily fall out of the basket.
- To prevent water dripping from the upper basket into the lower basket, empty the lower basket first, followed by the upper basket.

Function Of The Rinse Aid And Detergent The rinse aid is released during the final rinse to prevent water from forming droplets on your dishes, which can leave spots and streaks. It also improves drying by allowing water to roll off the dishes. Your dishwasher is designed to use liquid rinse aids. WARNING Only use branded rinse aid for dishwasher. Never fill the rinse aid dispenser with any other substances (e.g. Dishwasher cleaning agent, liquid detergent). This would damage the appliance. When to refill the rinse aid The regularity of the dispenser needing to be refilled depends on how often dishes are washed and the rinse aid setting used. Function of detergent The chemical ingredients that compose the detergent are necessary to remove, crush and dispense all dirt out of the dishwasher. Most of the commercial quality detergents are suitable for this purpose. WARNING - Proper Use of Detergent
  - Use only detergent specifically made for dishwashers use. Keep your detergent fresh and dry.
  - Don't put powdered detergent into the dispenser until you are ready to wash dishes. Dishwasher detergent is corrosive! Keep dishwasher detergent out of the reach of children.
